blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Enterprise risk in global trade is never the sum of individual trade risks. It is shaped by correlation — the uncomfortable reality that when things go wrong, they often go wrong together. A port congestion event may arrive the same week as a currency devaluation in the country served by that port and the collapse of a major buyer exposed to both. Each risk, in isolation, seemed modest. Together, they form a bad quarter.

Mature enterprise risk management builds a view of correlated scenarios, not just individual threats. What happens to us if three emerging markets weaken at once? If a major shipping lane closes for a month? If a sanctions list is expanded suddenly and we are holding exposure in the affected counterparties? These scenarios are stress-tested, costed, and then used to size the enterprise's capital buffer.

The uncomfortable lesson is that individual risks can be insured, but correlated shocks can only be survived. The role of enterprise risk is to make sure the company is in a position to survive them — not elegantly, but intact.

items.q: According to the text, enterprise risk is shaped primarily by…
options: the size of any single trade
items.why: "It is shaped by correlation — the uncomfortable reality that when things go wrong, they often go wrong together."

items.q: What are the correlated scenarios ultimately used for?
options: To size the enterprise's capital buffer
To replace the insurance programme entirely
To rank individual traders by performance
To choose which shipping lanes to use
items.why: "These scenarios are stress-tested, costed, and then used to size the enterprise's capital buffer."

items.q: The phrase "Each risk, in isolation, seemed modest. Together, they form a bad quarter" suggests that…
options: small risks are always safe to ignore
modest risks never need to be costed
the danger lies in risks arriving at the same time
items.why: Inferência: o perigo não está em cada risco, mas na coincidência deles — a correlação transforma pequenos em um trimestre ruim.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Stress-testing scenarios is more useful than listing single threats.
Correlated shocks demand a survivable capital position.
You can insure your way out of correlated shocks.
Enterprise risk is more than the sum of its parts.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma o contrário — "individual risks can be insured, but correlated shocks can only be survived".

items.q: The distinction between surviving "not elegantly, but intact" implies that…
options: elegance is the main measure of good risk management
the goal is to avoid all losses
the goal is endurance, even if the outcome is messy
correlated shocks can be prevented entirely
items.why: Inferência: o objetivo é sair inteiro do choque, mesmo que de forma feia — sobrevivência, não perfeição.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentar o stress test ao comitê de risco. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. Before I take you through the numbers, I want to be clear about what this slide is not. It is not a list of our biggest risks. Each of the three events on it would, on its own, be entirely manageable — we have handled worse.

What I am asking the committee to sit with is what happens when they land in the same fortnight. Picture it: a shipping lane through the strait is closed for repairs, the currency in our largest sourcing market is devalued overnight, and a mid-sized buyer — exposed to both — misses a payment. None of these is a crisis alone. Modelled together, correlated, they cost us roughly forty million and turn a decent quarter into a loss.

The point of the exercise is not to predict that exact week. It is to size the buffer that lets us absorb a week like it. My recommendation is that we hold the capital buffer at the higher figure until the sanctions picture settles. It will feel expensive right up until the quarter it isn't.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Sophie say the slide is NOT?
options: A proposal to cut the buffer
A summary of last quarter's losses
A list of the company's biggest risks
items.why: "It is not a list of our biggest risks."

items.q: What roughly is the combined, correlated cost of the three events?
items.why: "Modelled together, correlated, they cost us roughly forty million."

items.q: What is Sophie's recommendation to the committee?
options: Hold the capital buffer at the higher figure until the sanctions picture settles
Insure each of the three risks separately
Cut the buffer to reduce cost immediately
items.why: "My recommendation is that we hold the capital buffer at the higher figure until the sanctions picture settles."

items.q: When Sophie says the buffer "will feel expensive right up until the quarter it isn't," she means…
options: expenses will rise every quarter from now on
the cost only proves worthwhile once a bad quarter actually hits
the buffer should be cut before it becomes costly
the buffer will always look like wasted money
items.why: Inferência: o custo parece desperdício até o trimestre em que o choque acontece e a reserva salva a empresa.

items.q: What is the main purpose of Sophie's exercise?
options: To rank the three risks from worst to least severe
To size a buffer that can absorb such a combination
To predict the exact week the events will occur
items.why: Inferência: "The point of the exercise is not to predict that exact week. It is to size the buffer that lets us absorb a week like it."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board asked us to stress-test the portfolio against a simultaneous downturn." To stress-test means to…
options: examine performance under severe, hypothetical conditions
reduce the size of the portfolio
items.why: Stress-test = testar em estresse: ver como a carteira aguenta cenários extremos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We hold a ___ precisely so that a bad quarter does not become an existential one."
items.why: Capital buffer = reserva de capital que absorve os choques.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "An overnight ___ in the sourcing currency wiped out the margin on the whole shipment."
items.why: Devaluation = desvalorização da moeda, que corrói a margem.

items.q: "When two markets move together, we speak of correlation." Correlation here means…
options: the tendency of risks to move in step with one another
the legal relationship between two firms
the interest charged on a buffer
the total value of the exposure
items.why: Correlation = correlação: riscos que se movem juntos, o cerne da lição.

items.q: "The desk still had open exposure to several affected counterparties." These are…
options: the other parties in our contracts who are hit by the event
the shipping companies moving the cargo
items.why: Affected counterparties = contrapartes afetadas: as outras partes dos contratos atingidas pelo choque.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em comitês de risco. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the higher buffer." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "If the sanctions list expands, we may need to wind down our exposure to those names." To wind down means to…
items.why: Wind down = reduzir/encerrar de forma gradual e ordenada.

items.q: "Two members pushed back on holding so much idle capital." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente vetar de vez.

items.q: "When the shipping lane closed, the losses spilled over into the currency book." This means the losses…
options: spread from one area into another
items.why: Spill over = transbordar, contagiar outra área — a lógica da correlação.

items.q: "None of the individual hedges would move the needle on a correlated shock." This means they would…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, causar diferença perceptível.
